You are the SIMPLIFICATION reviewer in a /simplify pass. Repo: /home/nick/work/andesim. Do NOT hunt for correctness bugs. Only flag unnecessary complexity the diff ADDS: redundant/derivable state, copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code. Name the simpler form.

The diff under review (working tree, uncommitted):

1) driver/cmd_run.cpp -- abs_elf() gained an existence check:
  fs::path abs = fs::absolute(path, ec);
  if (ec) { fprintf(stderr, "andesim run %s: cannot resolve ELF '%s'\n", ctx, path); return ""; }
  if (!fs::is_regular_file(abs, ec)) { fprintf(stderr, "andesim run %s: ELF not found: %s\n", ctx, path); return ""; }
  return abs.string();
(previously it was `std::string abs = fs::absolute(path, ec).string(); ... return abs;`)

2) tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_missing_elf.sh -- NEW 53-line shell test:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "need build/andesim"
MISSING="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/__definitely_absent__.elf"
[ -e "$MISSING" ] && fail "test bug: $MISSING unexpectedly exists"
assert_missing() {
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" "$@" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "$label: missing ELF should exit non-zero, got 0: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi 'ELF not found' || fail "$label: missing the 'ELF not found' diagnostic: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'Unable to find the RISC-V BIOS' && fail "$label: reached qemu instead of failing in the driver: $out"
  ok "$label: missing ELF -> clean 'ELF not found', no engine spawn"
}
assert_missing "fast" run --mode fast "$MISSING"
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
export VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR"
eng=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null | awk '$2=="vsim"{print $1; exit}')
if [ -n "$eng" ]; then assert_missing "cycle" run --mode cycle --engine "$eng" "$MISSING"; else ok "SKIP cycle: ..."; fi
assert_missing "hybrid" run --mode hybrid "$MISSING"

Read tests/lib/log.sh and 1-2 sibling tests in tests/andes_sim/ (e.g. test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh) to judge whether the test's structure matches the established convention or adds needless complexity. Flag things like: the `grep ... && fail` pattern under `set -uo pipefail` (note: no `set -e`, and `&&` makes the line's exit status fine), redundant printf|grep when a simpler check exists, the [ -e "$MISSING" ] guard's value, comment verbosity.

Return a short findings list with file, line, one-line summary, simpler form. If nothing, say "clean". Be concise.

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env, then the legacy in-tree build dir.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v; v=$(cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$_LIB_ROOT/verilator/build"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F1+F3 (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md): the driver respects the ELF's class (rv32/rv64).
#   - fast  auto-picks qemu-system-riscv32/64 from the ELF (and runs it).
#   - cycle/hybrid reject an ELF whose class != the engine's xlen, both ways,
#     with one shared clear error and WITHOUT launching the engine.
# Independent, gated sections: rv64 always; the rv32 directions need
# HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 (build the rv32 fixture) and skip cleanly without it.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"   # fail/ok + cfg_val/vsim_bin_dir

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
elf=$(ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/handoff_roundtrip.elf 2>/dev/null \
      || ls "$ROOT"/tests/fixtures/*.elf 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -x "$BIN" ] && [ -n "$elf" ] || fail "need build/andesim + a fixture ELF"

BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)

# --- A. fast: an rv64 ELF auto-selects qemu-system-riscv64 (no --engine) ------
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --dry-run "$elf" 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'qemu-system-riscv64' \
  || fail "fast did not auto-pick riscv64 for an rv64 ELF: $out"
ok "fast: rv64 ELF -> qemu-system-riscv64"

# --- B. cycle: rv64 ELF on the rv32 engine (d23) -> clear error, no run -------
if [ -x "$BINDIR/sim_d23" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle \
        --engine vsim:d23 "$elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "cycle arch-mismatch should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv64 but engine 'vsim:d23' is rv32" \
    || fail "cycle arch-mismatch missing the clear error: $out"
  ok "cycle: rv64 ELF on vsim:d23 (rv32) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"
else
  ok "SKIP cycle rv64-on-rv32: no sim_d23 under $BINDIR"
fi

# --- C. rv32 directions: need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 to build an rv32 fixture -----
TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)}"
if [ -z "$TC32" ] || [ ! -d "$TC32/bin" ]; then
  ok "SKIP rv32 directions: HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 unset/unreachable"
  exit 0
fi
# Only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 -- the rv32 fixture build must not need the rv64 one.
make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$TC32" \
  >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "rv32 fixture build failed"
rv32elf="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rv32_c_hello.elf"
[ -f "$rv32elf" ] || fail "rv32 fixture missing after build: $rv32elf"

# fast: the rv32 ELF auto-selects qemu-system-riscv32.
out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --dry-run "$rv32elf" 2>&1)
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'qemu-system-riscv32' \
  || fail "fast did not auto-pick riscv32 for an rv32 ELF: $out"
ok "fast: rv32 ELF -> qemu-system-riscv32"

# fast: and it actually runs on qemu-system-riscv32 (rv32 runtime end to end).
QD=$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)
if [ -x "$QD/qemu-system-riscv32" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$rv32elf" 2>&1)
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'hello from QEMU1' \
    || fail "rv32 fixture did not run/print on qemu-system-riscv32: $out"
  ok "fast: rv32 fixture runs on qemu-system-riscv32 (rv32 runtime works)"
else
  ok "SKIP rv32 run: no qemu-system-riscv32 under $QD"
fi

# cycle: the rv32 ELF on an rv64 engine -> the reverse arch-mismatch error.
rv64eng=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null | awk '$2=="vsim" && $4=="64"{print $1; exit}')
if [ -n "$rv64eng" ]; then
  out=$(timeout 30 env VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR" "$BIN" run --mode cycle \
        --engine "$rv64eng" "$rv32elf" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "cycle rv32-on-rv64 should exit 2, got $rc: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "ELF is rv32 but engine '$rv64eng' is rv64" \
    || fail "cycle rv32-on-rv64 missing the clear error: $out"
  ok "cycle: rv32 ELF on $rv64eng (rv64) -> arch-mismatch error, no run"
else
  ok "SKIP cycle rv32-on-rv64: no rv64 vsim engine found"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# A missing ELF must fail in the driver with a clear "ELF not found", BEFORE any
# engine is launched -- never the cryptic downstream
# "qemu-system-riscv64: Unable to find the RISC-V BIOS ...".
# Covers fast (the reported case) + cycle; hybrid already guarded (regression).
# The fix lives at the one shared resolver (abs_elf), so fast/cycle/cycle-gdb
# all inherit it; this test pins fast + cycle + hybrid.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"   # fail/ok + cfg_val/vsim_bin_dir

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "need build/andesim"

MISSING="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/__definitely_absent__.elf"
[ -e "$MISSING" ] && fail "test bug: $MISSING unexpectedly exists"

# assert_missing <label> <args...>: run the driver, require a non-zero exit, the
# driver's own "ELF not found" diagnostic, and the ABSENCE of any engine spawn
# ("Unable to find the RISC-V BIOS" proves qemu was reached -- it must not be).
assert_missing() {
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  out=$(timeout 30 "$BIN" "$@" 2>&1); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "$label: missing ELF should exit non-zero, got 0: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qi 'ELF not found' \
    || fail "$label: missing the 'ELF not found' diagnostic: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'Unable to find the RISC-V BIOS' \
    && fail "$label: reached qemu instead of failing in the driver: $out"
  ok "$label: missing ELF -> clean 'ELF not found', no engine spawn"
}

# fast: the reported bug -- must not hand the missing path to qemu.
assert_missing "fast" run --mode fast "$MISSING"

# cycle: reaches the shared resolver only after engine discovery + selection, so
# it needs a concrete --engine (and VSIM_BIN_DIR for discovery). The existence
# check is arch-independent -- elf_xlen of a missing file is 0, so no arch
# mismatch fires first regardless of which engine we pick.
BINDIR=$(vsim_bin_dir)
export VSIM_BIN_DIR="$BINDIR"
eng=$("$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null | awk '$2=="vsim"{print $1; exit}')
if [ -n "$eng" ]; then
  assert_missing "cycle" run --mode cycle --engine "$eng" "$MISSING"
else
  ok "SKIP cycle: no vsim engine discoverable under $BINDIR"
fi

# hybrid: already validates existence up front -- regression guard.
assert_missing "hybrid" run --mode hybrid "$MISSING"

**tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_missing_elf.sh** — matches the sibling convention (arch_match) well: same boilerplate header, `printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q` checks, custom inline assertions rather than `expect` (the sibling does the same; `expect` can't express non-zero rc or a negative match, so a custom helper is justified, and it's reused 3x = good DRY).

Items the prompt flagged, judged:
- L31-32 `grep -q ... && fail` negative assertion: correct. No `set -e`, so grep's exit 1 on the good path doesn't abort; `fail` only fires on match. The `&&` one-liner IS the simpler form (an `if` block would be longer). It's also a distinct guarantee (no engine spawn) that the positive `ELF not found` check doesn't cover, so not redundant. Keep.
- L29 `printf | grep -qi`: identical to sibling convention, not redundant. Keep (a herestring would save a process but diverge from the established pattern).
- Header/inline comments: comment density is in line with the sibling (which also has a 7-line header). Not verbose by this repo's bar.

- **L19 `[ -e "$MISSING" ] && fail "test bug..."`** — low value. `__definitely_absent__.elf` is a literal sentinel nothing in the tree ever creates, so the guard protects an impossible state. Simpler form: drop the line. Harmless if kept (single line, same safe `&&`-under-no-`set -e` idiom), so optional.

Net: essentially clean. No copy-paste-with-variation, no derivable state, no dead code, no deep nesting introduced. The only removable line is the L19 existence guard, and that's a judgment-call nit, not a real complexity defect.
